title: Mayor
statement: Month seven of the West Oakland Stabilization Fund means another round of families staying in their homes instead of getting pushed out. We're not just cutting checks—we're walking blocks, knocking doors, making sure people who qualify know the fund exists. Brenda Okoro's team has this down to a system now: identify, verify, disburse, follow up. The canvass we launched last month is finding households who slipped through the cracks. That's the work—persistent, personal, Oakland. To the skeptics who said this would slow down or get buried in paperwork: look at the pace. We're ahead of where we projected. To West Oakland itself: this fund is yours. Built by Denise Carter's advocacy, delivered by this administration, sustained by the community organizers who make sure neighbors know their rights. Month seven is not a milestone to celebrate and coast. It's proof of concept that we can do this citywide. The Stabilization Fund was always meant to be more than a pilot. It's meant to be permanent. That's the fight ahead.
action: directed Brenda Okoro's housing unit to accelerate canvass operations in slipping blocks and prepare month-eight pipeline for early review
